Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Objective Arrest all 6 criminals with the highest score and win the game. Dice 2 blue dice (eye, eye, 2, 3, 4, 5) 2 black dice (eye, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5) 4 bandit dice (6 different bandits) Game Play Each player rolls 8 dice. 4 of the dice have the 6 criminals on them and the other 4 have number values from 1 (snake eye) to 6. You must split minimum of 1 die after each roll and re-roll the rest. That split die will not be rerolled again. At the end of your roll, you pick one of the criminals from your dice roll and arrest them. Scores are determined by the number of dice you have of that one criminal multiplied by the LOWEST number value. For example, if you rolled Clown, Clown, Clown, Fly, 2, 2, 4, 5. You will score 3 (clowns) x 2 (lowest numeric value) = 6. Or, if you choose Fly, you will score 1 (Fly) x 2 (lowest value) = 2. Twist: Snake Eye has value of 1 UNLESS you rolled 4 snake eyes, then it has a value of 7. If, at the end of your roll, you do not have a criminal dice face matching any of your unarrested criminals, you will have to choose any of your unarrested criminals, flip them over, and score 0 for that turn. Game ends after 6 turns. [Rating: 1/10] Just roll dice and pick the best ones to get as many points as possible with zero interaction.  It may be a good activity to complement a conversation but, when I play, I want TO PLAY.

[Rating: 1.5/10] Wenn man wirklich,wirklich gerne Würfel würfelt,ok...aber so dermaßen glückslastig. Kann man genau so gut ne Münze werfen.Gibt unzählige bessere kurze Spiele mit relativ hohem Glücksfaktor. Ein Teil meiner Wertung entspringt meinem unfassbarem Pech bei dem "Spiel",bei dem Versuch die "Erster Sieg"-Geschenkpunkte bei BGA zu bekommen. Wenn ich das irgendwann schaffe,müsste man mich schon gut bezahlen um dieses eklige Ding nochmal anzufassen.

[Rating: 2/10] Very bad game. No interaction with other players; when it's not our turn, we get bored.   We also get bored during our turn since the choices are ultimately quite predictable, and it doesn't get better as the matches go on because our viable choices become more and more limited. There is a missing gameplay element to add a touch of strategy and progression—why not special dices that we unlock/choose at the end of each round ?

[Rating: 3/10] Lukewarm Yahtzee derivative, terrible artwork, poor usability, heartwarmingly absurd setting. The Wurst result adds a nice "push your luck" element, which is rendered moot for actual methodical play by the uneven Wurst distribution on the indiscernible number dice. Any strategic options present in Yahtzee or similar games have been completely removed.

[Rating: 3/10] Potentially the "wurst" PYL dice chucker I've ever played. Look- I like Can't Stop, I'm definitely not opposed to a light, luck-heavy experience, but the choices here are as bland as can be and there is almost never any "payoff" but tons of let-down. Almost any Yahtzee roller is a better choice. Please play High Score or Martian Dice instead, I am seriously begging you. Very disappointed in the Brands this time.

[Rating: 3/10] Absolutely nothing special. Mechanics are already seen, in an abstract game that tries to hide it.

[Rating: 3/10] Super simple Yahtzee-like dice game - more like a children's game although it says 8+.  It's lacking any really push your luck - choices are obvious.  I would always pick Martian Dice over this one (or Wurfel Bohnanza for a bit more weight but it has the bonus you can score on opponent's turns).
